mainTopic: How big a blank gap between the text of a שטר and the witnesses makes it פסול, and whether a gap between the witnesses and the בית דין's approval is also a problem.
overview: The גמרא first asks whether the 'two lines' of blank space that make a שטר פסול include the space between the lines, and רב נחמן בר יצחק proves that they do. רבי שבתי, quoting חזקיה, adds that the lines are measured by ordinary handwriting like the witnesses', because a forger would not use a professional סופר. Three opinions then give the exact size of the gap. רב יצחק בן אלעזר says two lines and four spaces, like לך written over לך. עולא says two lines and three spaces, like a ל above and a ך below. רבי אבהו says one line and two spaces, like ברוך בן לוי on one line. Next, רב limits the gap rule to the space between the text and the עדים: a gap between the עדים and the בית דין's approval (אשרתא) is fine, as long as it is filled in with ink lines. The גמרא explains why ink lines help below the עדים but not above them, since a בית דין never signs on ink lines alone. The amud ends with a new challenge: a forger could cut off the top, erase the ink lines and write a fake שטר, which רב's own erasure rule would seem to allow.

steps.title: Do the two lines include the space between them?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether the 'two lines' gap counts only the written lines or also the blank space between lines.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does 'two lines' mean the lines together with their spaces, or maybe only the lines themselves without their spaces?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is asking how to measure the 'two lines' of blank space that make a שטר פסול. Do we count the space between lines too?
steps.deeperAnalysis: A line of writing has blank space above and below it. If that space counts, the gap needed to make the שטר פסול is bigger. If it doesn't count, a smaller gap is already enough to make it פסול.

keyTerms.meaning: Their spaces: the blank room between lines
Or perhaps: brings in the second side of a question

phrases.english: Them and their spaces,
phrases.notes: 'Them' means the two lines of writing, and 'their spaces' is the empty strip between one line and the next.

phrases.english: or perhaps them and not their spaces?

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵן וַאֲוִירָן, אוֹ דִלְמָא הֵן וְלֹא אֲוִירָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier discussion of the 'two lines' gap rule from the previous part of the daf.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the measurement of two blank lines includes the interlinear spaces.

steps.title: The spaces are included, by logic
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק argues that the measure must include the spaces, because one line without its space is useless anyway. The גמרא accepts this.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: It makes sense that it means the lines with their spaces. If you thought it means without their spaces, then what could one line without its space be used for? So we learn: the lines with their spaces. Yes, we learn this.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק answers the question with a logical argument, and the גמרא agrees with his conclusion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He argues backwards. If lines were measured without their spaces, then a gap of one such line could never hold any writing, so there would be no reason to talk about it at all. Since the rule does deal with it, the measure must include the spaces.

keyTerms.meaning: It stands to reason, it makes sense
If it entered your mind: introduces the opposite idea in order to reject it
Learn from this: a proof is accepted

steps.whatToRemember: The 'two lines' gap is measured as lines together with the spaces between them.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
It stands to reason that it means them and their spaces,
for if it would enter your mind
that it means them and not their spaces,
one line without its space,
what is it fit for?
phrases.notes: A single bare line with no room around it can't really hold forged writing, so there'd be no point in mentioning it.

phrases.english: Rather, learn from this: them and their spaces!
Learn from this.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק: מִסְתַּבְּרָא
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The measure is lines including their spaces, since one line without its space would be pointless to discuss.

steps.title: Measure by the witnesses' handwriting, not a scribe's
steps.stepSummary: רבי שבתי, quoting חזקיה, rules that the two lines are measured by the size of the witnesses' writing, because forgers do not use professional scribes.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שבתי said in the name of חזקיה: The two lines that the חכמים spoke about are measured by the handwriting of the witnesses, not the handwriting of a סופר. Why? Because anyone who forges does not go to a סופר to forge.
steps.whatsHappening: A new rule is added: how big is a 'line'? It is measured by ordinary handwriting like the witnesses', and the גמרא explains why.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A professional סופר writes small and neat, so he could squeeze more into a gap. But a forger would not hire a סופר. He would do it himself or use someone ordinary, so we measure by ordinary writing.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shabbtai said in the name of Chizkiya:
The two lines that they said,
phrases.notes: 'They' means the חכמים who ruled that a two-line gap makes the שטר פסול.

phrases.english: are measured by the handwriting of witnesses,
and not the handwriting of a scribe.
What is the reason?
Because anyone who forges,
does not go to a scribe and forge.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second detail about how to measure the two lines: whose handwriting size is used.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The two lines are measured by ordinary (witnesses') handwriting, since forgers do not use professional scribes.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the measure is built around how a real forger would act.

steps.title: How much space is needed?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the exact size of the gap, including the spaces.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up the next move. It asks for the exact measurement of the two lines with their spaces.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We already know the spaces count. Now the גמרא wants to know how many spaces and how big, so there is a clear size.

phrases.english: And how much?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on step 2 (spaces are included) and asks for the exact amount.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The precise size of the gap of two lines with their spaces.

steps.title: Enough room for 'לך' written above 'לך'
steps.stepSummary: רב יצחק בן אלעזר gives the size: enough room to write the word לך twice, one above the other.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יצחק בן אלעזר said: For example, 'לך' and 'לך', this one on top of that one.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יצחק בן אלעזר answers with a picture: room for the word לך written twice, one under the other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The letter ל sticks up above the line and the final ך drops below it. So writing לך over לך takes up the two lines and also the space above and below each one.

keyTerms.meaning: The word 'to you': a ל going up and a final ך going down
This one on top of that one

phrases.english: Rav Yitzchak ben Elazar said:
For example, 'lecha' and 'lecha,'
phrases.notes: He picked לך because the ל reaches up and the final ך reaches down, so each word fills the space above and below it.

phrases.english: this one on top of that one.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יִצְחָק בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר: כְּגוֹן
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The gap equals the room needed to write לך above לך.

steps.title: Two lines and four spaces
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא draws out what רב יצחק בן אלעזר must hold: the gap is two lines plus four spaces.
steps.simpleTranslation: It seems he holds: two lines and four spaces.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains what רב יצחק בן אלעזר's example means in numbers: two lines and four spaces.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each לך uses a space above it (for the ל) and a space below it (for the ך). Two words, each with two spaces, adds up to four spaces along with the two lines.

keyTerms.meaning: He holds, he is of the opinion

steps.whatToRemember: A gap that makes a שטר פסול is measured in ordinary handwriting, and per רב יצחק בן אלעזר it is two lines plus four spaces, like לך written over לך.

phrases.english: Apparently he holds:
two lines and four spaces.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the measurement implied by the example in step 5.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: According to רב יצחק בן אלעזר, the gap that makes the document פסול is two lines with four spaces.

steps.title: עולא's measure: a ל above and a final ך below
steps.stepSummary: רב חייא בר אמי, quoting עולא, gives a different size for the gap: enough room for a ל on an upper line and a final ך on a lower line.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חייא בר אמי said in the name of עולא: for example, enough room for a ל on the upper line and a final ך on the lower line.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a second answer to the question from step 4: how big exactly is the gap? עולא gives his own picture, different from רב יצחק בן אלעזר's "לך twice."
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of writing a whole word twice, עולא pictures two lines with just one letter each. The ל goes on the top line and the final ך goes on the bottom line. The size of the gap is set by how much room those two letters need.

keyTerms.meaning: The final form of the letter כ (ך), whose tail drops down

phrases.aramaic: רַב חִיָּיא בַּר אַמֵּי מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּעוּלָּא אָמַר:
phrases.english: Rav Ḥiyya bar Ami said in the name of Ulla:
For example, a lamed on the upper line
and a khaf on the lower line.
phrases.notes: This is the final כ (ך), the one with the long tail.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב חִיָּיא בַּר אַמֵּי מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּעוּלָּא אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer to the step 4 question, competing with רב יצחק בן אלעזר's answer in step 5.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The exact size of the gap, spaces included (from step 4).
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Enough room for a ל on the upper line and a final ך on the lower line.

steps.title: So עולא holds: two lines and three spaces
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא works out that עולא's picture adds up to two lines with three spaces.
steps.simpleTranslation: So he must hold: two lines and three spaces.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws out what עולא's example means as a measurement: two lines plus three spaces.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יצחק בן אלעזר needed two lines and four spaces. עולא's picture comes out one space smaller: two lines and three spaces. That makes it a real disagreement about the size of the gap, not just different wording.

keyTerms.meaning: Apparently; so it comes out that
Three blank spaces (between or around lines)

phrases.english: Apparently he holds:
two lines and three spaces.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns עולא's letter example into a measurement, the same way step 6 did for רב יצחק בן אלעזר.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: For עולא, the forbidden gap is two lines and three spaces, one space less than רב יצחק בן אלעזר.

steps.title: רבי אבהו's measure: "ברוך בן לוי" on one line
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו gives a third size: enough room to write the name ברוך בן לוי on a single line.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said: for example, "ברוך בן לוי" written on one line.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a third answer to the step 4 question. רבי אבהו pictures one line holding the name ברוך בן לוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This name also has a final ך (in ברוך) and a ל (in לוי), like עולא's example. The difference is that רבי אבהו puts them on one line instead of two, so his gap is smaller.

keyTerms.meaning: A sample name; it contains both a final ך and a ל

phrases.english: Rabbi Abbahu said:
For example, "Barukh ben Levi"
on one line.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third competing answer to the step 4 question, after steps 5 and 7.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The exact size of the gap, spaces included (from step 4).
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Enough room for the name ברוך בן לוי on one line.

steps.title: So רבי אבהו holds: one line and two spaces
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא works out that רבי אבהו's picture adds up to one line with two spaces.
steps.simpleTranslation: He holds: one line and two spaces.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws out what רבי אבהו's example means as a measurement: one line plus two spaces.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the smallest of the three sizes. To sum up: רב יצחק בן אלעזר says two lines and four spaces, עולא says two lines and three spaces, and רבי אבהו says one line and two spaces.
steps.whatToRemember: Three opinions on the forbidden gap: רב יצחק בן אלעזר: 2 lines + 4 spaces; עולא: 2 lines + 3 spaces; רבי אבהו: 1 line + 2 spaces.

phrases.english: He holds:
one line and two spaces.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns רבי אבהו's example into a measurement, matching the pattern of steps 6 and 8.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: For רבי אבהו, the forbidden gap is one line and two spaces, the smallest measure of the three.

steps.title: רב: the rule applies only to a gap between the text and the witnesses
steps.stepSummary: רב rules that the gap rule applies only between the text and the עדים. A gap between the עדים and the בית דין's approval (אשרתא) does not make the שטר invalid, even if it is large.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: they only taught this about a gap between the עדים and the text. But between the עדים and the אשרתא, even a large gap is still valid.
steps.whatsHappening: רב opens a new point: he limits where the gap rule applies. Only a gap above the עדים' signatures, between them and the text, is a problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some שטרות have an אשרתא, an approval by a בית דין that is written below the עדים' signatures. רב says a blank space between the עדים and that approval does not make the שטר invalid, no matter how big it is.

keyTerms.meaning: They only taught this about... (limits a rule)
The written text of the שטר
A בית דין's approval of the שטר, written below the עדים' signatures

phrases.english: Rav said: They taught this only
about a gap between the witnesses and the text,
but between the witnesses and the court's ratification,
even a large gap is also valid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the size of the gap to where the gap rule applies.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The gap rule applies only between the text and the עדים. A gap between the עדים and the אשרתא, even a big one, leaves the שטר valid.
steps.whyThisMatters: It sets the boundaries of the whole gap rule, and the next steps will test whether that boundary makes sense.

steps.title: Why is a gap before the court's approval any safer?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב: the forgery fear behind the gap rule seems to apply just as much to a gap between the עדים and the אשרתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is different about a gap between the עדים and the text? There we fear he will forge, write whatever he wants, and the עדים are already signed. But between the עדים and the אשרתא too, he can forge, write whatever he wants, and have עדים sign!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב's rule from step 11. It says the same forgery danger exists in both places, so why treat them differently?
steps.deeperAnalysis: A gap above the עדים is banned because a forger could fill it with new text that the real עדים seem to back up. The גמרא argues that a forger could also fill a gap below the עדים, writing his own lines and getting other עדים to sign there, with the בית דין's approval below seeming to cover it all. So רב's distinction looks unjustified.

keyTerms.meaning: What is different? (asks why two cases are treated differently)

phrases.english: What is different about between the witnesses and the text?
Perhaps he will forge and write whatever he wants,
and the witnesses are signed;
between the witnesses and the ratification too,
he can forge and write whatever he wants,
and have witnesses sign!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly challenges רב's distinction from step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling that a gap between the עדים and the אשרתא does not make the שטר invalid.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The reason for the gap rule is fear of forgery. That fear seems to apply equally to a gap below the עדים, so there is no basis for treating it differently.

steps.title: The gap is fine when it is filled in with ink lines
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that רב's leniency covers only a gap between the עדים and the אשרתא that has been filled in with ink lines.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is when he fills in the gap with ink lines.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from step 12. רב allows a gap between the עדים and the אשרתא only when someone has filled that gap in with ink lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry was that someone could write something extra in the empty space. If the space is covered with ink lines (טיוטא), nothing can be added there, so the forgery fear is gone.

keyTerms.meaning: fills in a blank space with ink lines or marks
the ink lines or marks that fill a blank space

phrases.english: When he fills it in with ink lines.
phrases.notes: The empty gap between the עדים and the בית דין's approval gets covered with lines, so nothing can be added there.

steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב allows any gap between the עדים and the אשרתא, even an open one, which invites forgery.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב only allows a gap that has been filled in with ink lines, so nothing can be added.

steps.title: Why not use ink lines for the gap above the עדים too?
steps.stepSummary: If ink lines solve the problem, they should also solve a gap between the text of the שטר and the עדים.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, let him also fill in the gap between the עדים and the שטר with ink lines!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer it just gave. If ink lines fix a gap, why does the basic rule demand that the עדים sign close to the text? Just fill that gap with ink lines too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The basic gap rule invalidates a שטר when there is a large space between the text and the עדים. If ink lines stop forgery below the עדים, they should work just as well above the עדים. Then that rule would seem unnecessary.

phrases.english: If so, between the witnesses and the document
let him also fill it in with ink lines!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, בֵּין עֵדִים לַשְּׁטָר נָמֵי מְטַיֵּיט לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer in step 13 by applying it to the main gap rule
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If ink lines remove the forgery fear, they should also fix a gap between the text and the עדים. Then the strict gap rule would not be needed.

steps.title: People might think the עדים signed only on the ink lines
steps.stepSummary: Ink lines above the עדים do not help, because people might say the עדים signed only to confirm the ink lines, not the text.
steps.simpleTranslation: People would say: the עדים signed only on the ink lines.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that ink lines cannot fix a gap between the text and the עדים. If the עדים sign right under ink lines, people might think they were signing only about those lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The עדים must clearly be signing on the text itself. If ink lines sit between the text and their signatures, their signatures look connected to the lines and not to the actual deal. So the gap rule still stands.

phrases.english: They would say: the witnesses signed only on the ink lines.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Pointing out a different concern that the fix creates
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Ink lines could replace the requirement that the עדים sign close to the text.
steps.terutzMaskana: Ink lines above the עדים create confusion about what they signed on, so they do not help.

steps.title: The same doubt should apply to the בית דין
steps.stepSummary: Then a filled-in gap between the עדים and the אשרתא should be a problem too, since people might say the בית דין signed only on the ink lines.
steps.simpleTranslation: Between the עדים and the אשרתא too, people would say: the בית דין signed only on the ink lines!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the last answer back on רב. If ink lines confuse what the עדים signed on, they should also confuse what the בית דין signed on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב's leniency depends on ink lines filling the gap below the עדים. The same reasoning from step 15 would mean the בית דין's approval looks tied only to the ink lines. Then רב's case would fail.

keyTerms.meaning: the court's written approval of a שטר

phrases.english: Between the witnesses and the court's approval too,

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרִי: בֵּי דִינָא אַטְּיוּטָא הוּא דַּחֲתִימִי!
phrases.english: they would say: the court signed only on the ink lines!

steps.triggerLanguage: בֵּין עֵדִים לָאַשַּׁרְתָּא נָמֵי, אָמְרִי: בֵּי דִינָא אַטְּיוּטָא הוּא דַּחֲתִימִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the reasoning of step 15 against רב's case from step 13
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling, as explained in step 13
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If ink lines make the עדים's signatures look tied only to the lines, they should do the same to the בית דין's approval.

steps.title: A בית דין never signs on ink lines alone
steps.stepSummary: A בית דין does not sign just to confirm ink lines, so nobody would make that mistake about its approval.
steps.simpleTranslation: A בית דין does not sign on ink lines.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the comparison does not work. Everyone knows a בית דין signs to approve the whole שטר, never just some ink lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עדים might sign on small details, so their signatures can be misread. A בית דין's approval is always about the whole document, so the ink lines cannot cause confusion. רב's ruling stands.

phrases.english: A court does not sign on ink lines.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing between עדים and בית דין
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The בית דין's approval could be misread as being only about the ink lines.
steps.terutzMaskana: A בית דין only signs on a whole שטר, so there is no confusion.

steps.title: A new forgery worry: cut, erase, rewrite
steps.stepSummary: Someone could cut off the original text, erase the ink lines, write a fake text with new עדים, and it would be valid under רב's own ruling about erasures.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us worry that he might cut off the top part, erase the ink lines, write whatever he wants and have עדים sign it. And רב said: a שטר whose text and עדים are written on an erased spot is valid!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new challenge against רב's leniency. Even with ink lines, a forger could turn the filled-in gap into a brand-new fake שטר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The forger cuts off the original text and its עדים, keeping only the inked gap and the בית דין's approval below it. He erases the lines, writes a new text and adds new עדים. Normally an erased spot would look suspicious, but רב himself rules that a שטר whose text and עדים are both on an erased spot is valid. So the בית דין's approval would seem to back the fake.

keyTerms.meaning: an erased spot on the paper

steps.whyThisMatters: This challenge sets two of רב's rulings against each other: the gap rule with ink lines, and the rule that a שטר written over an erasure is valid.

phrases.english: But let us worry that perhaps he cuts off the top part,
phrases.notes: He cuts off everything above the inked gap, the real text and the original witnesses, keeping only the inked gap and the court's approval.

phrases.english: and erases the ink lines,
and writes whatever he wants, and has witnesses sign;

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַב: שְׁטָר הַבָּא הוּא וְעֵדָיו
phrases.english: and רב said: a document that comes with its text and its witnesses
on an erased spot is valid!
phrases.notes: This is a separate ruling of רב.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises a new forgery concern against רב's ink-line leniency after step 17 defended it
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling that a filled-in gap between the עדים and the אשרתא is acceptable
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ink lines can be erased and replaced with a fake text and new עדים. רב's own ruling validates a שטר written over an erasure, so the forgery would succeed.
